title: Safety, moderation, identity and regulation for virtual worlds in 2026
summary: The 2025–2026 regulatory environment has converged on a single operating model for any user-to-user virtual world: a pseudonymous public identity bound to a privately verified or estimated age band, with minors defaulted into locked-down settings and adult content hard-gated behind "highly effective" checks. Roblox is the bellwether: after Louisiana, Kentucky and Texas AG suits (Aug–Nov 2025) it made facial age estimation (Persona, six age bands, adjacent-band chat only) mandatory for chat globally from January 2026, and by September 2026 had paid roughly $54m in state settlements (WV, AL, NV $35.8m; MS; SD ~$10m; KS $9.8m) that contractually bind it to age verification and adult-to-under-16 contact limits, with five more suits pending. The UK OSA age-check duty applied 25 July 2025 and Ofcom has fined six adult operators (£500k–£1.35m each) always paired with a second fine for failing to evidence compliance; the EU's DSA Article 28 guidelines (14 July 2025) treat self-declaration as unreliable and come with a prototype wallet-based age app; Australia's under-16 ban (10 Dec 2025) covers ten social platforms but explicitly excludes Roblox, Discord and Steam as gaming-purpose services, while warning the list is not static. US federal bills (KIDS Act passed House 267–117 on 29 June 2026; KOSA cleared Senate Commerce 5 Aug 2026) are still not law. Age verification created its own liability: Discord's outsourced appeals vendor leaked ~70,000 ID images (Sept–Oct 2025). VR harassment has a ten-year evidence trail (2016 groping, Meta's always-on 4-ft Personal Boundary Feb 2022, UK police's non-prosecutable 2024 "virtual rape" probe, Sept 2025 Senate whistleblower testimony), and Meta is removing Horizon Worlds from VR on 15 June 2026. Moderation at scale is AI-first: Roblox's Sentinel caught 35% of grooming cases proactively and drove ~1,200 NCMEC reports in H1 2025 against 24,522 reports in 2024, while combined safety+infra spend rose 26% to $1.15bn. Economy rules are settled by precedent: Second Life banned chance-based wagering on 25 July 2007; Steam banned blockchain/NFT games 15 Oct 2021; SEC's 2023 NFT actions ($500k, $1m) still stand despite 2025 softening; Belgium (2018, Jan 2025) treats paid tradeable loot boxes as gambling while the Dutch Council of State (9 Mar 2022) exempted skill-game loot boxes. EU AI Act Article 50 labelling applies from 2 Aug 2026; NO FAKES Act 2026 is pending; EAA applies to storefronts/apps from 28 June 2025. Method caveat: WebFetch was blocked by the egress proxy, so primary pages were read through search excerpts.
design_implications: Ship age-banding at account creation from day one: pseudonymous public identity plus a private age band from on-device facial estimation or a wallet/credential proof (EU age app); never store ID images centrally; design appeals without document upload where possible (Discord's 70k-ID leak came from the appeals vendor).

Default-restrict minors per DSA Article 28 guidelines and the Roblox settlement template: adjacent-age-band-only chat, private profiles, no stranger voice/DMs, geolocation off, no engagement notifications, parent-managed accounts for under-16s with world/contact/spend approval.

Hard-gate adult regions behind Ofcom-grade 'highly effective' age checks tied to the credential, inheriting Second Life's General/Moderate/Adult region ratings but replacing the opt-in checkbox with verified eligibility; geo-fence adult content and economy features by jurisdiction.

Build embodied-safety primitives into the engine: always-on personal boundary (user-adjustable radius), one-gesture mute/block/vanish, instance owner kick/lock, and a short rolling session buffer attached to abuse reports so VR assaults are evidentiable (UK police found a 2024 case non-prosecutable).
Use behaviour-earned trust ranks (VRChat model) to gate uploads, scripting, voice and proximity rights; show a nuisance flag; do not award rank for idle time, low-effort uploads or mass-friending.

Make proactive AI detection the primary moderation layer with published metrics (NCMEC reports, proactive-catch rate) and treat audit logs, retention policies and regulator information-request SLAs as product features, since Ofcom fines un-evidenced compliance separately.

Economy rules: no chance mechanics that pay out transferable or cash-out-able value (Second Life's 2007 rule); odds disclosure and under-18 consent for any random reward; no blockchain tokens or NFTs, which forfeit Steam distribution and invite Howey analysis; design item transferability deliberately because Belgium and Washington treat tradeable items as gambling stakes.

Biometric minimisation: process eye, face and hand tracking on-device, transmit only abstracted animation data, obtain explicit consent, publish retention/deletion policy, never sell or ad-target on gaze (Colorado HB 24-1130, Illinois BIPA exposure).

AI-content governance: machine-readable provenance on every AI-generated asset plus a perceptible in-world 'AI' label (EU AI Act Art. 50 from 2 Aug 2026); likeness consent registry and DMCA-style takedown/counter-notice for digital replicas so the platform is NO FAKES/TAKE IT DOWN ready.

Decide nolife's declared primary purpose (creation/play vs social networking) with Australia's 'age-restricted social media platform' test in mind, and make the storefront, account and support flows EAA-compliant from launch (in force 28 June 2025).
open_questions: Will Australia's eSafety designate Roblox or social VR worlds as age-restricted platforms, given the FAQ says the list is not static?
Which of the KIDS Act (H.R. 7757) or KOSA (S. 1748) becomes US law in 2026–27, and does state-law preemption survive?
Does facial age estimation meet Ofcom's 'highly effective' bar at 16/18 thresholds, and what buffer band and error rates are accepted?
When will the EU Digital Identity Wallet age credential be live and accepted, making on-platform estimation unnecessary in the EU?
Will any court hold that gaze/eye-tracking data is a biometric identifier under Illinois BIPA?
Does the NO FAKES Act of 2026 pass, and how will its safe harbour treat user-made avatars resembling real people?
Did Linden Lab change Second Life's UK adult-content verification after the 25 July 2025 OSA deadline? (Not found.)
What are the full-year 2025 Roblox NCMEC figures and the outcomes of the pending Texas, Florida, Tennessee, Iowa and Nebraska suits?

Full-text verification of several primary pages (Roblox newsroom, eSafety FAQ, EC press release, Ofcom report) was not possible because the egress proxy blocked fetches; those facts rest on search-engine excerpts of the pages.

claims.claim: Roblox made facial age estimation (via Persona) required to access chat globally from January 2026, sorting users into six bands (under 9, 9–12, 13–15, 16–17, 18–20, 21+) with chat limited by default to adjacent bands; enforcement began December 2025 in Australia, New Zealand and the Netherlands.

checks.note: Consistent with Roblox's 18 Nov 2025 announcement and Jan 2026 rollout: Persona facial age estimation (ID/parental consent fallback), bands <9/9-12/13-15/16-17/18-20/21+, default chat limited to similar/adjacent bands, enforced early Dec 2025 in Australia, New Zealand and the Netherlands, then globally early Jan 2026. Caveat: no live source could be fetched this session (search budget exhausted, egress proxy 403); verdict rests on checker's prior knowledge. Nuance: requirement covered chat only; estimation is probabilistic with ID-based correction.

Matches Roblox newsroom posts of 18 Nov 2025 (announcement) and 7 Jan 2026 (global rollout): Persona facial age estimation required for chat; six bands (under 9, 9-12, 13-15, 16-17, 18-20, 21+); default chat with same/adjacent groups; under-9 chat off without parental consent; first enforced Dec 2025 in Australia, New Zealand and the Netherlands. Primary page not fetchable this run (DNS failure); verdict from checker knowledge.

claims.claim: Roblox settled with West Virginia ($11.1m), Alabama ($12.2m) and Nevada ($12.5m) for $35.8m total on 21 April 2026 over child-safety claims; Kansas ($9.8m, Sept 2026), South Dakota (~$10m, July 2026) and Mississippi (June 2026) followed, while Texas, Florida, Tennessee, Iowa and Nebraska suits remained pending.

checks.note: No web access this session and most items (Jun-Sep 2026) are post-cutoff. Independently known: AG suits by Louisiana (Aug 2025), Kentucky (Oct 2025), Texas (Nov 2025), Florida (Dec 2025), Iowa and Nebraska (early 2026), plus a federal MDL in N.D. Cal. (Dec 2025). The WV/AL/NV $35.8m settlement and later KS/SD/MS figures are single-source (Bloomberg/state press) and must be re-checked before use; the brief's '$54m+' total is its own arithmetic.

Settlement dates (Apr-Sep 2026) are at or after the checker's knowledge horizon and the Bloomberg page could not be fetched. Figures are internally consistent (11.1+12.2+12.5 = 35.8; with Kansas 9.8 and South Dakota ~10 the brief's '$54m+' holds). Pre-2026 litigation history (Louisiana Aug 2025, Kentucky Oct 2025, Texas Nov 2025) is correct. Treat per-state amounts as single-source.

claims.claim: Under the UK Online Safety Act, age-check duties applied from 25 July 2025; Ofcom fined AVS Group £1m plus £50k (Dec 2025), Kick Online Entertainment £800k plus £30k and 8579 LLC £1.35m (Feb 2026), each paired with a separate penalty for failing to answer information requests; maximum fines are £18m or 10% of global turnover.

checks.note: Core facts hold: age-check duty from 25 Jul 2025 and £18m / 10% qualifying worldwide revenue cap are correct; AVS Group £1m + £50k (Dec 2025) matches memory of Ofcom's first age-assurance fine. Kick Online Entertainment £800k+£30k and 8579 LLC £1.35m (Feb 2026) are plausible but could not be checked. Missed context: Ofcom's earliest OSA fines were information-request penalties against 4chan (Oct 2025) and Itai Tech (Nov 2025), so the paired-fine pattern predates age-check enforcement.

Partly confirmed from knowledge: age-assurance duties from 25 Jul 2025; max penalty £18m or 10% of qualifying worldwide revenue; AVS Group Ltd £1m plus £50k information-request penalty (Dec 2025). The Feb 2026 Kick Online Entertainment (£800k+£30k) and 8579 LLC (£1.35m) figures could not be checked. Precision flaw: claim says 'each paired' with an information-request penalty but gives no paired amount for 8579 LLC. Source is a law blog, not Ofcom.

claims.claim: As of 10 December 2025 Australia's under-16 ban applies to Facebook, Instagram, Kick, Reddit, Snapchat, Threads, TikTok, Twitch, X and YouTube, and eSafety lists Roblox, Discord, Steam/Steam Chat, LEGO Play, Messenger and WhatsApp as not meeting the 'age-restricted social media platform' definition because gaming/messaging is their primary purpose.

checks.note: Matches eSafety's list of ten age-restricted platforms (obligations from 10 Dec 2025) and its not-restricted assessments (Discord, GitHub, Google Classroom, LEGO Play, Messenger, Pinterest, Roblox, Steam/Steam Chat, WhatsApp, YouTube Kids) under the statutory carve-out for services whose sole/primary purpose is messaging, gaming, education or health. Nuance: eSafety reassesses continuously and had floated adding Roblox; platform penalties up to A$49.5m.

Matches eSafety's 5 Nov 2025 statement and FAQ: ten age-restricted platforms from 10 Dec 2025 (Facebook, Instagram, Kick, Reddit, Snapchat, Threads, TikTok, Twitch, X, YouTube); Roblox, Discord, Steam/Steam Chat, LEGO Play, Messenger, WhatsApp (plus GitHub, Google Classroom, YouTube Kids, later Pinterest) listed as not meeting the definition because gaming/messaging/education is the sole or primary purpose. eSafety says the list is not static.

claims.claim: The European Commission published DSA Article 28 guidelines on protection of minors and a prototype privacy-preserving age-verification app on 14 July 2025, applying to all platforms accessible to minors (not just VLOPs) and treating self-declared age as unreliable.

checks.note: Date (14 Jul 2025, IP/25/1820), content and 'not only VLOPs' framing are right, and self-declaration is deemed not appropriate. Correction: the guidelines do not apply to ALL platforms accessible to minors — micro and small enterprises are exempt (Art 19 DSA) unless designated VLOPs — and they are non-binding (Art 28(4)). The age-verification app is a 'blueprint' piloted in Denmark, France, Greece, Italy and Spain; guidelines favour estimation generally and verification for 18+ content.

Commission press release of 14 Jul 2025 published the Art 28(1) DSA guidelines on protection of minors and the age-verification app prototype (piloted with Denmark, France, Greece, Italy, Spain). Guidelines apply to all online platforms accessible to minors, not only VLOPs, and treat self-declaration as inadequate. Caveat omitted by the claim: micro and small enterprises are exempt.

claims.claim: Discord confirmed that a breach of a third-party support vendor (attacker access 22–24 September 2025, disclosed 3 October 2025) exposed government-ID images of approximately 70,000 users who had submitted age-related appeals; attackers' claim of 2.1 million IDs is disputed by Discord.

checks.note: Discord disclosed on 3 Oct 2025 (update 8 Oct) that a third-party support vendor (5CA, Zendesk-based ticketing) was compromised, ~70,000 users may have had government-ID photos from age appeals exposed; attackers claimed 1.5 TB / 2.1m IDs, which Discord called inflated extortion. Caveat: Discord said it detected and revoked access on 20 Sep 2025; the 22-24 Sep / 58-hour window is the attackers' account and should be marked contested, not company-confirmed. 5CA denied its systems were breached.

Discord disclosed on 3 Oct 2025 and on 8 Oct 2025 said approximately 70,000 users may have had government-ID photos exposed via a third-party support vendor (named as 5CA, which disputed being the entry point); attackers claimed ~2.1m photos / 1.5 TB / 5.5m users, which Discord called inaccurate. Exact access window (22-24 Sep, 58 hours) could not be re-checked; some reports placed access around 20-24 Sep. Cited source is a security news site, not Discord's own post.

claims.claim: Roblox's open-sourced Sentinel system contributed about 1,200 NCMEC reports in H1 2025 and 35% of detected child-endangerment cases were caught proactively; Roblox filed 24,522 NCMEC reports in 2024 (0.12% of 20.3m total).

checks.note: Roblox's Aug 2025 Sentinel post reports ~1,200 NCMEC reports in H1 2025 and ~35% of cases detected proactively; 24,522 NCMEC reports for 2024 is from Roblox's 15 Aug 2025 letter to the Louisiana AG. Minor denominator wobble: NCMEC's 2024 CyberTipline total is usually reported as ~20.5m, not 20.3m (0.12% share unchanged). All figures are company-reported and unaudited; Sentinel ran on text chat only.

Matches Roblox's 7 Aug 2025 Sentinel post (about 1,200 NCMEC reports in H1 2025; 35% of detected child-endangerment cases caught proactively) and its 15 Aug 2025 response letter (24,522 NCMEC reports in 2024). Denominator note: NCMEC's published 2024 CyberTipline total is about 20.5m reports, not 20.3m; either way the share is 0.12%.

claims.claim: Meta introduced an always-on 'Personal Boundary' of roughly four feet (two-foot radius per avatar) in Horizon Worlds and Venues on 4 February 2022 after groping reports; in March 2026 Meta announced Horizon Worlds would be removed from VR on 15 June 2026 and survive only as a mobile app.

checks.note: Personal Boundary announced 4 Feb 2022 with ~4 ft separation (2 ft per avatar). Nuance: it was 'always-on' only at launch — Meta made it user-adjustable (off / 2 ft / 4 ft) in March 2022, so the mandatory framing is dated. The March 2026 announcement removing Horizon Worlds from Quest on 15 Jun 2026 (mobile-only survival) is consistent with Meta's early-2026 Reality Labs retrenchment but could not be re-fetched this session; lower confidence on that half.

First half confirmed: Meta shipped the default-on Personal Boundary (~4 ft between avatars, 2 ft radius each, no haptics) in Horizon Worlds and Venues on 4 Feb 2022. The March 2026 announcement that Horizon Worlds leaves VR on 15 Jun 2026 and survives only as a mobile app is at the edge of the checker's horizon and the CNBC page could not be fetched; it is consistent with Meta's late-2025 metaverse budget cuts and Jan 2026 Reality Labs layoffs but is single-source here.

claims.claim: Valve banned applications built on blockchain technology that issue or exchange cryptocurrencies or NFTs from Steam on 15 October 2021 as an extension of its rule against items with real-world value; the SEC's Impact Theory (28 Aug 2023, $500k) and Stoner Cats (13 Sept 2023, $1m) NFT settlements remain in force despite the SEC's 2025 position that digital collectibles are generally not securities.

checks.note: Steam's blockchain/NFT prohibition surfaced 14-15 Oct 2021 and Stoner Cats' $1m penalty (13 Sep 2023) is right. Correction: Impact Theory (28 Aug 2023) was not a $500k settlement — $500k was the civil penalty within a ~$6.1m total (disgorgement + prejudgment interest + penalty), plus destruction of unsold tokens and removal of royalty code. The 2025 SEC retreat (Crypto Task Force; OpenSea and Yuga Labs probes closed early 2025; Peirce/Atkins 'digital collectibles are not securities' position) is real and neither 2023 order has been vacated, so 'remain in force' holds.

Valve's Steam rule against blockchain/NFT apps was reported 15 Oct 2021 (after Age of Rust's removal), framed as an extension of the no-real-world-value rule. SEC: Impact Theory 28 Aug 2023 ($500k civil penalty, but total order over $6.1m with disgorgement and interest); Stoner Cats 2 LLC 13 Sep 2023 ($1m civil penalty); Peirce and Uyeda dissented in both. The 2025 SEC shift (Project Crypto; closed OpenSea/Yuga Labs probes) does not vacate the consent orders. The Akin Gump source covers only the SEC actions, not Valve.

claims.claim: The EU AI Act Article 50 transparency duties (machine-readable marking by providers; perceptible deepfake labels by deployers) apply from 2 August 2026, with final Commission guidelines published 20 July 2026 and about 190 signatories to the voluntary Code of Practice by end of July 2026.

checks.note: 2 Aug 2026 is the statutory application date for AI Act Art 50 (confirmed). The 20 Jul 2026 final guidelines date and ~190 signatories are post-cutoff and could not be checked. Omitted nuance: the Commission's Digital Omnibus proposal (19 Nov 2025) would delay the Art 50(2) marking duty for generative systems placed on the market before 2 Aug 2026 until 2 Feb 2027; adoption status must be verified before relying on the 2 Aug 2026 date for existing systems. Code of Practice drafts: Dec 2025 (first), Mar 2026 (second).

The 2 Aug 2026 application date for Art 50 is correct (AI Act Art 113), as is the provider-marking vs deployer-labelling split. The 20 Jul 2026 final-guidelines date and ~190 Code of Practice signatories are after the checker's horizon and the Paul Weiss memo could not be fetched. Omission: the Commission's Digital Omnibus on AI (19 Nov 2025) proposed deferring the Art 50(2) marking duty for generative systems placed on the market before 2 Aug 2026 to 2 Feb 2027; its adoption status should be checked.

additional_findings: Method limitation: no independent web evidence was obtainable this session — the shared WebSearch budget (200/turn) was already exhausted and every WebFetch/HTTPS egress attempt returned 403/ENOTFOUND via the proxy. Verdicts rest on the checker's prior knowledge (reliable to ~mid-2026); all post-June-2026 claims are unverifiable and should be re-checked in a session with working search.

App-store-level age verification is arriving independent of platform choices: Utah's App Store Accountability Act (effective May 2025), Texas SB 2420 (scheduled 1 Jan 2026, preliminarily enjoined Dec 2025), and Apple's Declared Age Range API already hand apps an age band; a successor world distributed via mobile stores must be able to consume a store-supplied age signal.

The DSA minors guidelines exempt micro and small enterprises (unless VLOP) and are non-binding; a small launch team is not immediately bound, but the guidelines become the Digital Services Coordinator's yardstick as the service grows.

Private litigation is the larger Roblox exposure: hundreds of grooming/CSAM suits were centralised into a federal MDL (N.D. Cal., Dec 2025), several naming Discord as co-defendant because the harm pathway was world-to-Discord DM migration; off-platform contact prompts should be treated as a detection signal.

Discord's breach vector was the outsourced support/appeals ticketing system (5CA on Zendesk), which also exposed names, emails, partial payment data and support transcripts — the support stack, not the age-estimation model, is the crown-jewel surface.
Meta's Personal Boundary became user-adjustable (off/2ft/4ft) within weeks of launch in March 2022; the transferable design lesson is default-on and user-controllable, not mandatory.

Ofcom's first Online Safety Act penalties were for ignoring information requests (4chan Oct 2025; Itai Tech Nov 2025) before any age-check fine, so a regulator-response function with audit trails is a day-one requirement.

The EU Digital Omnibus proposal (Nov 2025) would push AI Act Art 50(2) marking for pre-existing generative systems to Feb 2027, so the AI-provenance deadline is politically fluid and should be tracked.

Australia's regime carries penalties up to A$49.5m per breach and eSafety has stated the platform list is reassessed continuously; gaming platforms with substantial social features can be re-designated, so 'framing as a game' is mitigation, not a safe harbour.

Verification limits this run: WebFetch failed DNS for every cited host, the shared WebSearch budget was already exhausted before the first query, and a curl probe via the proxy was denied; no workaround was attempted. Verdicts rest on checker knowledge through mid-2026 and internal consistency, not on fresh fetches. Claims 1, 7 (second half) and 9 (second half) should be re-checked when web access is available.
EU DSA Art 28 minors guidelines exempt micro and small enterprises (DSA Art 19), so an early-stage successor world may fall outside them until it scales; design for compliance from day one anyway.

US COPPA Rule amendments (final Jan 2025, effective 23 Jun 2025, compliance deadline 22 Apr 2026) tighten consent for third-party disclosure and impose data-retention limits; any under-13 age band triggers them.

US app-store age-verification laws (Texas SB 2420 effective 1 Jan 2026 but preliminarily enjoined Dec 2025; Utah effective May 2026; Louisiana Jul 2026) push age signals to the OS/app-store layer; a successor should be built to consume app-store/OS age signals and EU wallet credentials rather than running its own ID-upload flow.

NCMEC's 2024 CyberTipline total (~20.5m) fell from 36.2m in 2023 because of report bundling, so year-on-year platform report ratios are not comparable; use incident counts, not report counts, for safety KPIs.
Discord's 2025 ID exposure came through the human appeals channel at a vendor (5CA), not the automated estimation path; appeals should avoid raw document upload and vendor-side retention.
Impact Theory's total SEC order exceeded $6.1m (disgorgement plus $500k penalty), so the deterrent against marketing digital items for price appreciation is larger than the brief's figure implies.

The Digital Omnibus on AI proposal may defer the AI Act Art 50(2) machine-readable marking duty for pre-existing generative systems to 2 Feb 2027; confirm its status before scheduling compliance work for AI-generated avatars, assets or NPC speech.
